facts.fact: Adwave's checklist says a small business's primary conversion should be one action, and that in practice four action types (calls, form leads, bookings, purchases) cover most local and online businesses.
facts.quote: In practice, four actions cover most local and online businesses:

facts.fact: Google Ads groups conversions into three categories: website actions, app actions, and phone calls and offline sales.
facts.quote: Google Ads groups conversions into website actions, app actions, and phone calls and offline sales.

facts.fact: Adwave's example suggests a plumber might set a minimum phone call length of 60 seconds so that short wrong-number or robocall contacts are not counted as conversions.
facts.quote: A plumber might set 60 seconds, since a real service request takes longer than that.

facts.fact: Calls to a forwarding number only count as conversions when they last at least the minimum call length the advertiser sets.
facts.quote: only calls lasting at least the minimum length you set count as conversions

facts.fact: Per the University of Minnesota's UTM guidelines, UTM tracking requires three fields: source, medium, and campaign.
facts.quote: require three fields: source, medium, and campaign

facts.fact: Most website conversion tracking uses two pieces: a base tag that loads on every page and an event snippet that fires when the conversion happens.
facts.quote: Most website tracking uses two pieces.

facts.fact: For lead businesses, the suggested value per qualified call is an estimate calculated as average job value multiplied by close rate.
facts.quote: multiply your average job value by your close rate to get a value per qualified call

facts.fact: Adwave's checklist states that reported conversions from browser-based tags are a floor because ad blockers and browser privacy features can block them, so undercounting should be expected.
facts.quote: Your reported conversions are a floor.

facts.fact: Google's guidance, as summarized on the Adwave page, is to wait 4 to 6 hours after creating a new offline conversion action before the first upload.
facts.quote: Wait 4 to 6 hours after creating a new offline conversion action before the first upload.

facts.fact: According to the walkthrough the page cites (ivitskiy.com, a third-party source), uploading before the waiting period can delay conversions by 2 days.
facts.quote: Uploading sooner can delay conversions by 2 days, according to the same walkthrough.

facts.fact: Google's developer documentation states that imported offline conversion statistics can take up to three hours to appear for last-click attribution.
facts.quote: imported conversion statistics can take up to three hours to appear for last-click attribution

facts.fact: Imported offline conversions are reported under the impression date of the original click, not the date of the import request.
facts.quote: they’re reported for the impression date of the original click, not the date of the import request

facts.fact: Per the Attribi review, Google labels file-based offline conversion uploads a legacy feature, and no end date has been published for them.
facts.quote: Google labels file-based uploads a legacy feature, though no end date has been published.

facts.fact: The Google Ads API upload has been closed to developer tokens that have no upload history, effective since June 15, 2026.
facts.quote: The Google Ads API upload has been closed to developer tokens with no upload history since June 15, 2026.

facts.fact: Adwave's pricing page lists a $30/day minimum for TV, Google (Search included), Facebook and Instagram.
facts.quote: TV, Google (Search included), Facebook and Instagram run from the $30/day minimum

facts.fact: Adwave's pricing page says TikTok starts at $91/day and must be turned on before use.
facts.quote: while TikTok starts at $91/day and needs to be turned on
